    Selected work

    Evidence-grounded agent systems

    The work moves from measured decisions to model structure, agent behavior, constraint checks, and consequences in a coupled environment.

    Selected work

    From a problem to inspectable evidence

    A plausible AI decision is not necessarily a realistic or valid one. I compare it with human evidence, check its limits, and trace what happens next.

    01

    People and their environment

    Human surveys inform behavioral models; simulated households make adaptation choices under flood and resource constraints.

    Evidence

    02

    Evidence-linked scientific work

    AI research agents handle literature and tasks. I build tools that make sources, validation checks, and workflow state inspectable.

    Evidence

    Four roles, kept apart

    Human respondents
    Real people whose survey answers provide the human evidence.
    Simulated household agents
    Model households that make adaptation choices in FLOODABM; they are not people and not an LLM system.
    LLM decision agents
    Language models that answer survey questions or propose actions. I compare their answers with human evidence (manuscript in preparation) and, in WAGF (in development), check proposals before a simulation changes.
    AI research agents
    Software that handles literature and tasks, while sources, checks, and workflow state stay inspectable.

    These projects share a research approach, not one integrated published system.

    01

    Human-Grounded LLM Evaluation

    Evaluation
    Why
    Can AI-generated flood-insurance answers reflect how real households make decisions?
    How
    I compared real household surveys with profile-based LLM responses using measurement checks, decision-pathway analysis, and repeated runs.
    Contribution
    A way to detect differences in household variation and decision relationships that average answers alone can hide.

    View case study: Human-Grounded LLM EvaluationPublic sourceRelated research profile

    Methods and boundaries
    Methods
    Evaluation design · Psychometrics and SEM · Stability analysis
    Boundaries
    The interactive examples use synthetic records, not individual survey responses or research results.
    02

    FLOODABM

    Simulation
    Why
    How do household choices change flood losses and the resources available next year?
    How
    I built the household decision model and connected adaptation choices to catastrophe, insurance, and financial mechanics.
    Contribution
    A traceable link from household adaptation choices to losses, insurance outcomes, and resources in later years.

    View case study: FLOODABMPublic sourceWater Resources Research article

    Methods and boundaries
    Methods
    Agent-based modeling · Coupled simulation · Risk systems
    Boundaries
    Simulated household agents model adaptation; they are not an integrated LLM system.
